title: Automating the SDLC
objective: Track changes through artifacts, validation, approval, phased delivery, and rollback.

sections.title: Making the pipeline a record of change
paragraphs: DevOps professionals do not treat source, builds, tests, artifacts, and environment promotion as separate manual tasks. For each run, they associate the input commit, dependencies, generated artifacts, execution role, test results, and approver, tracking which changes were delivered to which environments.

AWS CodePipeline is a continuous delivery service that models, visualizes, and automates the steps required for releases. Success is not defined solely by the pipeline completing; quality gates and post-deployment observation conditions are also included.

sections.title: Promote Only Verified Artifacts
paragraphs: Place tests where they can detect failures early for each purpose: unit, integration, acceptance, and security testing. Rebuilding separately for each environment can result in what was verified differing from what is deployed to production, so promote the same immutable artifact through the stages.

Associate dependency vulnerabilities, image contents, signatures, licenses, and test results with the artifact. Do not bypass failed checks solely through approval; record the scope, reason, expiration date, and approver for every exception.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Automated Testing and Artifacts

sections.title: Limiting the Impact of Changes with Progressive Delivery
paragraphs: For production releases, identify the candidate and stable versions, and compare quality, latency, error rate, and business metrics for a limited group of users or amount of traffic. Define the conditions for continuing and stopping in advance, and if an anomaly occurs, roll back to a known-good version.

How to read the diagram: Solid request and response lines represent the data plane, while the approval, metrics, and rollback elements at the top represent the control plane. Before increasing the percentage directed to the candidate version, compare the metrics for the candidate and stable versions for the same operation.

checkpoints.prompt: The release manager for the payment API wants to demonstrate that the code executed in production is identical to the code that passed the approved tests. Choose one most appropriate design for the delivery record.

choices.text: Rebuild from the same source separately for each environment, without recording differences in the generated artifacts.
choices.explanation: The validated artifact may differ from the production artifact.

choices.text: Record only the manual copy to production.
choices.explanation: This cannot demonstrate the relationship between the tests and the artifact.

choices.text: Link the commit, test results, signed immutable artifact, approvals, and environment promotions in a single delivery record.
choices.explanation: The same validated artifact can be tracked through to production.

checkpoints.prompt: An artifact that failed a vulnerability scan for its dependencies must be distributed temporarily as an emergency fix. Choose the single most appropriate exception-handling measure.

choices.text: Permanently disable vulnerability scanning across the entire pipeline.
choices.explanation: Future changes will no longer be detected.

choices.text: Record the exception’s scope, reason, expiration date, and approver, then rerun the same scan after remediation.
choices.explanation: This keeps the scan enabled while managing accountability and the exception’s expiration.

choices.text: Delete the failed result and send only the artifact to production.
choices.explanation: The risk and rationale for the decision cannot be tracked.

checkpoints.prompt: Immediately after deploying the candidate version to 5% of the traffic, only the candidate version exceeded the error-rate threshold. Based on the stopping conditions for the phased deployment, select one most appropriate next action.

choices.text: Do not increase the allocation to the candidate version; revert to the known-good version and compare the logs and metrics for the same operation.
choices.explanation: This follows the stopping conditions, limits the impact, and investigates the cause.

choices.text: Deploy the candidate version to all traffic without investigating the cause.
choices.explanation: This expands the impact on users.

choices.text: Stop monitoring the error rate and check it after the deployment is complete.
choices.explanation: This defeats the purpose of validating the phased deployment.
